rounds.note: sRGB encode fixed; staged background, rolled camera
guard, steel, pommel land; rot now the loudest fault
light cut 10x; rot desaturated; real speculars appear
rot rebuilt in value; all primary metrics in range for the first time
lighting rebalanced by ablation; beam, ground contact, horizon event
brightness ceiling retired; beam, lit floor, contact shadow at 3.75%
wear + anisotropy contracts exercised by all four part modules

p1.gap: Parry hooks are the wrong idea, not badly sized — any bilateral widening within a blade-width of the guard reads as a second guard at any scale. Delete them and reclaim the length.

p2.gap: Wear and aniso now set, but the exposed apex was tuned as a near-mirror assuming rot would cover it — it now reads blown. Agent was mid-taming when the session limit hit.

p3.gap: Saturation 0.62->0.36 and coverage now reaches mid-blade, but the wear contract is unexercised — no part module sets s.wear, so the hold-back never engages.

p4.gap: Wear mask fires and the sculpt survives, but the worn metal is speckly and reads brassy rather than knocked-clean iron. High-frequency normal noise needs cutting.

p5.gap: Fittings now legible and wear/aniso set. Warm key is catching the ferrule lip as orange arcs — the agent identified these as its own, not the rot's.

p6.gap: Wear and aniso set. Gem exemption in place but the emission-fade hack that masked the ragged girdle has not been verified as removable yet.

p7.gap: Value structure is lengthwise only — the flat reads as one value across its width, because the slot pitch is coarser than the few degrees of azimuth a near-flat blade sweeps sideways.

p8.gap: Background range 3.7x->5.8x and the desaturation test now passes unaided, but the staging reads as hard flat diagonal bands competing with the weapon rather than as a room.
